name: Learning and Training Methods
text:
# Learning and Training Methods
## Overview
This family covers methods for learning and training 3D [Gaussian splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) representations from 2D images [G]. It focuses on optimizing primitive parameters (positions, covariances, opacities, colors) and network weights through [differentiable rendering](#16276-differentiable-rendering.md) pipelines [G]. It is distinguished from sibling methods like [Splatting Without the Blur](1157-splatting-without-the-blur.md) by its reliance on gradient-based learning rather than purely analytical initialization, and from [Rendering Pipelines and Passes](1411-rendering-pipelines-and-passes.md) by its focus on the [training loop](#4290-training-loop.md) rather than inference [rasterization](#15310-rasterization.md) [G].
## Shared principles
All methods in this family rely on differentiable rendering to compute gradients from the rendered image to the Gaussian parameters (position, covariance, opacity, [spherical harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md)) and/or network weights [G]. The rendering process remains differentiable with respect to the scene representation [G]. Loss functions typically combine photometric reconstruction error, such as $\mathcal{L}_{L1}$ or $\mathcal{L}_{MSE}$, with perceptual or structural metrics like $\mathcal{L}_{MS-SSIM}$ or $\mathcal{L}_{LPIPS}$ [G].
## Subtopics

### [Gaussian Avatar Reconstruction](1575-gaussian-avatar-reconstruction.md)
[Gaussian Avatar Reconstruction](#1575-gaussian-avatar-reconstruction.md) refers to a family of methods that reconstruct animatable, photorealistic 3D human or head avatars by representing them as collections of 3D Gaussians [1575-gaussian-avatar-reconstruction.md]. Unlike static scene reconstruction, these methods must handle non-rigid deformation, ensuring that the Gaussian primitives move and deform consistently with the underlying subject's pose and expression [1575-gaussian-avatar-reconstruction.md]. The family is distinguished from static Gaussian Splatting [946-gaussian-splatting.md] by its integration of parametric body models (e.g., SMPL, FLAME) or deformation fields to constrain and drive the Gaussian positions, and from [neural radiance field (NeRF)](#834-neural-radiance-field-nerf.md) avatars by its explicit, rasterizable representation that enables real-time rendering speeds [1575-gaussian-avatar-reconstruction.md].

A core principle is the anchoring of Gaussians to a geometric prior. Most methods initialize Gaussians on the surface of a parametric mesh (e.g., SMPL for full body, FLAME for heads) in a canonical rest pose [1575-gaussian-avatar-reconstruction.md]. During training, these Gaussians are deformed to match the target pose using rigid transformations (e.g., Linear Blend Skinning) and/or non-rigid deformation fields [1575-gaussian-avatar-reconstruction.md]. This ensures that the avatar can be animated to novel poses while maintaining structural integrity [1575-gaussian-avatar-reconstruction.md].

### [Pose-free and Feed-forward Training](6500-pose-free-and-feed-forward-training.md)
This family encompasses methods that reconstruct [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) scenes directly from input images without iterative per-scene optimization or reliance on pre-computed [Structure-from-Motion (SfM)](#16341-structure-from-motion-sfm.md) pipelines [6500-pose-free-and-feed-forward-training.md]. Unlike traditional 3DGS which requires minutes to hours of per-scene optimization using known camera poses, these methods use feed-forward neural networks or geometry priors to generate primitives and camera parameters in seconds [6500-pose-free-and-feed-forward-training.md]. They are distinguished from sibling methods like [Gaussian Avatar Reconstruction](1575-gaussian-avatar-reconstruction.md) by their focus on generalizable scene reconstruction from static, unposed image collections rather than animatable human models [6500-pose-free-and-feed-forward-training.md].

### VS-Splat with GenDen Augmentation
[VS-Splat](#8542-vs-splat.md) integrated with the GenDen add-on model [S1, unofficial]. On CO3D dataset, VS-Splat + GenDen yields PSNR 22.09, SSIM 0.865, LPIPS 0.208 [S1, unofficial].
